fields.event: index in the match's events (= match.json events)
fields.frame: frame index in the half at the site's rate (fps)
fields.frame_src: frame index in the half at the source rate (fps_src)
fields.carrier: player index (match.json players) of the passer
fields.target: player index of the receiver the passer chose (given or inferred)
fields.best: the coach's best option: kind (pass / carry / shot), target player (pass) or angle in degrees (carry, relative to the attacking direction)
fields.rank: rank of the chosen pass among all options by coach score (1 = the coach's best)
fields.p_chosen: success probability of the chosen pass
fields.p_best: success probability of the best option
fields.score_chosen: coach score of the chosen pass (expected change of the net xG)
fields.above_median: score(chosen) - median score of the options, expected goals
fields.third: pitch third of the passer (defensive / middle / attacking, for the passing team)
fields.outcome: within horizon_s: goal / shot by the passing team, else kept / lost (pass completed or not)
fields.net_xg: xG of the passing team minus xG against within horizon_s

caveats: Everything here is the model's opinion. A missed opportunity means the model valued another option more, not that the player made a mistake.
The value model is weak: on held-out matches it explains about 2 % of the variance of the net xG in the next 15 s, little more than 'closer to the goal is better'.
The coach is bolder than professional players: its top-ranked options are riskier, and pros complete more of the passes it ranks lower.
Only passes the event sync placed on the tracking are included (about two thirds of open-play passes in the Bundesliga data); the intended receiver of a failed pass is inferred from the ball's path.
Player and team numbers need at least 20 decisions; below that they are flagged too_few.
